preamble: Fronting of the voiced postalveolar affricate [dʒ] to the alveolar affricate [dz] is a common result of loanword adaptation in languages that have /dz/ but no /dʒ/. In Modern Greek, Turkish, Italian and English loans with [dʒ] are written ⟨τζ⟩ and pronounced /dz/. Sardinian treats Italian [dʒ] the same way. Native sound changes of the same kind mostly start from retroflex /dʐ/ (Polish mazurzenie: jeżdżę > [jɛzd͡zɛ]), which belongs in a separate retroflex dʐ→dz cell.

examples.note: Loanword adaptation; Greek has no native /dʒ/ and substitutes /dz/.
Borrowed from Italian with [dʒ] adapted as [dz].
